title: Zero-touch batch & quant optimizer with rollforward safety fence
author: Aisha Kline
description:
Motivation: Many customers ask for low-effort cost tuning that is safe for production. This PR introduces a "zero-touch" optimizer that can propose and optionally apply batch/caching defaults and quantization profiles on a per-tenant basis, driven by telemetry signatures and unit-econ heuristics. The goal is automated, reversible improvements with clear safety fences and rollforward capabilities.

What this PR does (single-string sectioned summary):
- Adds a cost-orchestrator service component (cost-orch) that consumes sampled workload traces and generates candidate configurations (batch_size, max_latency_slo, cache_prefix_rules, quant_profile) using a rule-based + lightweight ML heuristic.
- Introduces a rollforward safety fence: any auto-applied config runs in shadow mode for N minutes and then is applied incrementally with traffic shaping and automatic rollback triggers based on error rate, latency regressions, or quality-signature drift.
- Provides per-tenant dry-run and tenant-scoped policy overrides (opt-out, max-quant-level, min-accuracy-threshold).
- Exposes a CLI dry-run mode and a Console API endpoint for suggestions listing + one-click apply.
- Adds telemetry markers and new metrics to support explainability: cost_delta_estimate, expected_latency_change, quality_risk_score.

Checklist: [x] design doc linked, [x] unit tests, [x] e2e smoke, [x] CI linting, [x] canary rollout plan in release notes.

Design notes: The optimizer is deliberately conservative — it favors batching and cache rules before applying quantization changes. Quantization is applied as a graded rollforward (INT8 -> Q4_0 -> Q4_1 as appropriate) with A/B shadow comparisons to ensure no silent quality regressions. The cost-orch runs off sampled traces from the workload-sampler and uses historical KV-cache hit distributions to compute benefit windows.

Testing and rollout: Local unit tests and a dedicated e2e job were added. We ran a staged canary on internal tenant "sandbox-ops" for 72h (see canary report attached) and observed median token-cost reduction 18% with P99 latency within SLO. Automated rollback triggered once for a synthetic anomaly and performed as designed.

Risks and mitigations: Risk: an overly aggressive quant profile could cause hallucination spike on structured outputs. Mitigation: quality_risk_score threshold and structured-output validators; policy opt-out for tenants with regulated outputs. Risk: config churn. Mitigation: dedupe window and minimum-stable-duration for auto-applied configs.

Related: references ENG-2034 (heuristic cost advisor), SUP-4124 (support request: tenant saw cost spike), and UX ticket PM-558 describing Console UX for suggestions.

Release plan: merge to main, enable feature-flag gated rollout, enable for 5 internal tenants for the next sprint, then gradual 10% tenant ramp per week with telemetry gating.
